sources.text:
The Bardenas Reales (in Basque: Errege Bardea) is a semi-desert natural region, or badlands, of some 42,000 hectares (420 km2; 104,000 acres) in southeast Navarre (Spain). The soils are made up of clay, chalk, and sandstone and have been eroded by water and wind creating surprising shapes, canyons, plateaus, tabular structures, and isolated hills, called cabezos. Bardenas Reales lacks urban areas, vegetation is scarce and the many streams that cross the territory have a markedly seasonal flow, staying dry most of the year.
The area has been a natural park since 1999 and a UNESCO biosphere reserve since 2000. Since 1951 part of it has been used as an air weapons range by the Spanish Air Force.


== Location ==
The Bardenas is in the southeast of Navarre, bordering Aragon. It is located in the middle of the depression of the Ebro valley at the foot of the mountains of the Yugo and the Zaragoza region of Cinco Villas. It is about 45 km (28 mi) from north to south and 24 km (15 mi) east-west, at an altitude ranging between 280 and 659 m (919 and 2,162 ft). Its area is 41,845 hectares (418.45 km2; 103,400 acres). It borders thirteen Navarrese municipalities: Carcastillo, Santacara, Mélida...
